extracted.intended_audience: Math 216 students (advanced undergraduates / beginning graduate students in algebraic geometry)
extracted.subtask_description: Study and exercise-focused guidance on construction and properties of tensor/symmetric/exterior algebras, finiteness notions (finite type, finitely presented, coherent), torsion/torsion-free sheaves, rank, determinant line bundles, and basic line bundles O(n) on projective space. Includes definitions, propositions, exercises, and useful hints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor algebra T•(M)
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is an A-module, then the tensor algebra T•(M) is a noncommutative algebra, graded by Z≥0, with T0(M)=A, Tn(M)=M ⊗A ··· ⊗A M (n factors), and multiplication given by concatenation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the starting point for Sym•M and ∧•M; A-subscript (T•A(M)) is usually omitted. Exercises reference sheafified versions T•F.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetric algebra Sym• M
rubrics_metrics.description: Sym• M is the quotient of T•(M) by the two-sided ideal generated by elements enforcing full symmetry of tensor factors (i.e., relations m1⊗· · ·⊗mn = mσ(1)⊗· · ·⊗mσ(n) for permutations σ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symn M is quotient of M⊗n by permutations; can also be characterized by a universal property: any map symmetric in entries factors uniquely through SymnA(M). Sheafified version Symn F introduced for quasicoherent sheaves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exterior algebra ∧•M
rubrics_metrics.description: ∧•M is the quotient of T•M by the two-sided ideal generated by all elements of the form x⊗x for x∈M, giving skew-commutativity relations m1⊗· · ·⊗mn − (−1)sgn(σ)mσ(1)⊗· · ·⊗mσ(n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 2 is invertible in A (e.g., char ≠ 2), ∧nM is the quotient of M⊗n by alternating relations. Can be defined by universal properties; sheafified to ∧•F.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheafified tensor/symmetric/exterior constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: For a quasicoherent sheaf F, one can define quasicoherent sheaves TnF, Symn F, and ∧nF by describing them on affine opens and using the characterization of quasicoherent sheaves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If F is locally free of rank m, then TnF, Symn F, and ∧nF are locally free; exercise asks to find their ranks. These constructions extend to O-modules on arbitrary ringed spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtration of Symr F in short exact sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Given 0 → F' → F → F'' → 0 of locally free sheaves, for any r there is a filtration Symr F = G0 ⊃ G1 ⊃ ··· ⊃ Gr+1 = 0 with subquotients Gp/Gp+1 ≅ (Symp F') ⊗ (Symr−p F'').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints: interpret transition matrices as block upper triangular, or reduce to an affine open where sheaves are free and check localization behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtration of ∧r F in short exact sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose 0 → F' → F → F'' → 0 is exact with locally free sheaves; for any r there is a filtration ∧r F = G0 ⊃ G1 ⊃ ··· ⊃ Gr+1 = 0 with subquotients Gp/Gp+1 ≅ (∧p F') ⊗ (∧r−p F'').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In particular, if sheaves have finite rank then det F = (det F') ⊗ (det F''). Use this to prove determinant multiplicativity in exact sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perfect pairing of exterior powers
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is locally free of rank n, there is a natural map ∧r F × ∧n−r F → ∧n F called a perfect pairing of vector bundles (generalizing perfect pairings of vector spaces).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise suggests using this pairing in later applications (e.g., duality of Hodge numbers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determinant line bundle det F
rubrics_metrics.description: For a locally free sheaf F of rank n, ∧n F is denoted det F and called the determinant (line) bundle or determinant locally free sheaf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determinant behaves well in exact sequences (alternating product of determinant bundles is trivial); see Exercise 13.5.H and hints to break exact sequences into short exact sequences and apply filtrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Torsion-free module/sheaf
rubrics_metrics.description: An A-module M is torsion-free if am = 0 implies either a is a zero-divisor in A or m = 0. Over an integral domain A this means am = 0 only if a = 0 or m = 0. An OX-module F is torsion-free if all stalks Fp are torsion-free OX,p-modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define torsion submodule Mtors as elements annihilated by some nonzero element; M is torsion-free iff Mtors = 0. Warning: notion called 'strictly torsion-free' in some sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Torsion quasicoherent sheaf on a reduced scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: A quasicoherent sheaf on a reduced scheme is torsion if its stalk at the generic point of every irreducible component is 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used mainly for coherent sheaves on regular curves where the notion is simple; referenced Exercise 13.7.G for consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasicoherent sheaf of ideals ↔ closed subscheme
rubrics_metrics.description: A sheaf of ideals is quasicoherent iff it comes from a closed subscheme. For a closed embedding i: X ↪ Y, there is a surjection OY → i_* OX whose kernel IX/Y is a sheaf of ideals, giving the exact closed subscheme sequence 0 → IX/Y → OY → i_* OX → 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare to earlier exercises characterizing quasicoherent sheaves; an example of a non-quasicoherent ideal was given earlier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finiteness notions for modules: finitely generated, finitely presented, coherent
rubrics_metrics.description: Finitely generated: there is a surjection A⊕p → M. Finitely presented: there exists an exact sequence A⊕q → A⊕p → M → 0. Coherent: M is finitely generated and any map A⊕p → M has finitely generated kernel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If A is Noetherian these three notions coincide. Exercises show implications (coherent ⇒ finitely presented ⇒ finitely generated) and discuss subtlety in non-Noetherian contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherent sheaf on a scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: A quasicoherent sheaf F is finite type / finitely presented / coherent if for every affine open Spec A, Γ(Spec A, F) is a finitely generated / finitely presented / coherent A-module. On a locally Noetherian scheme the three notions agree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coherent sheaves on X form an abelian category CohX. Checking finite typeness/coherence can be done on a single affine cover via Affine Communication Lemma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associated points of coherent sheaves
rubrics_metrics.description: Associated point theory for coherent sheaves on a locally Noetherian scheme parallels the affine case; associated point of a scheme means associated point of OX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Properties and terminology referenced to earlier section 5.5; embedded points defined similarly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hom(F, G) quasicoherent when F coherent
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is a coherent sheaf on X and G is quasicoherent, then Hom(F, G) is quasicoherent. If additionally G and OX are coherent, Hom(F, G) is coherent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof via describing on affine opens and localization properties; left-exactness statements: Hom(F, · ) is left-exact QCohX → QCohX and Hom(· , G) left-exact CohX^op → QCohX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duals and reflexivity of coherent sheaves
rubrics_metrics.description: If OX is coherent and F is coherent, then the dual F∨ := Hom(F, OX) is coherent. The natural map F → (F∨)∨ (double dual map) is not always an isomorphism; coherent sheaves for which it is an isomorphism are called reflexive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: coherent sheaf from k[t]/(t) on A1 has dual 0, illustrating failure. The canonical map F ⊗ F∨ → OX is called the trace map.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hom(F, G) for finite rank locally free F
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is finite rank locally free and G is quasicoherent, there is an isomorphism Hom(F, G) ≅ F∨ ⊗ G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generalizes the vector-bundle case; exercise asks to describe this isomorphism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exactness of Hom sequences with locally free terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an exact sequence of quasicoherent sheaves 0 → H → G → F → 0 where H is locally free and E any quasicoherent sheaf, the induced sequence 0 → Hom(H, E) → Hom(G, E) → Hom(F, E) → 0 is exact (right-exactness holds here).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local argument reduces to free-module splitting; consequently dual sequences 0 → H∨ → G∨ → F∨ → 0 hold when terms are coherent and H locally free.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support of finite type quasicoherent sheaf is closed
rubrics_metrics.description: The support (where germs are nonzero) of a finite type quasicoherent sheaf on a scheme X is a closed subset; the support of a general quasicoherent sheaf need not be closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof reduces to affine case using finite set of generators; references Exercise 2.4.2 and 2.6.F(b) for definitions. On locally Noetherian schemes, nilpotent sheaf is coherent hence has closed support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric Nakayama (generators of fiber generate locally)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a scheme and F a finite type quasicoherent sheaf, and sections a1,...,an in F(U) map to generators of the fiber F|p := Fp/mp Fp at p, then there exists an affine neighborhood Spec A of p such that those sections generate F|Spec A as an A-module, and generate all stalks and fibers in that neighborhood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses Nakayama's Lemma and localization arguments; immediate corollary: if Fp ⊗ κ(p) = 0 then F is zero on some neighborhood of p.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local freeness is a stalk-local property for coherent sheaves
rubrics_metrics.description: For a coherent sheaf F on X, if Fp is a free OX,p-module at some p, then F is locally free in some neighborhood of p. Hence F is locally free iff all stalks are free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses Geometric Nakayama to find generators, then shows kernel has closed support not containing p; remove support to obtain isomorphism with O^n. Consequence: on integral schemes coherent sheaves are locally free on a dense open set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Torsion and torsion-free sheaves on regular curves
rubrics_metrics.description: On a regular (locally Noetherian) curve, torsion-free coherent sheaves are locally free; torsion coherent sheaves are supported at finitely many closed points; any coherent sheaf F has a canonical exact sequence 0 → F_tors → F → F_lf → 0 with F_tors torsion and F_lf locally free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce to discrete valuation ring case and use structure theorem for finitely generated modules over PID; refer to Remark 12.5.15.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rank of a quasicoherent sheaf at a point
rubrics_metrics.description: The rank of a quasicoherent sheaf F at p is rank_p(F) := dim_{κ(p)} (Fp/mp Fp), the dimension of the fiber over the residue field. On affine Spec A with module M, rank is dim_{K(A/p)} Mp/pMp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If F is finite type the rank is finite and equals the minimal number of generators of Mp by Nakayama. For irreducible X, 'rank F' by convention means rank at the generic point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upper semicontinuity of rank for finite type sheaves
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is a finite type quasicoherent sheaf on X, then rank(F) is an upper semicontinuous function on X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved using Geometric Nakayama: generators at a point yield generators nearby. Example earlier shows finite type hypothesis is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constant rank on reduced scheme implies local freeness
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is reduced and F a finite type quasicoherent sheaf with constant rank n, then F is locally free of rank n. Consequently, on an integral scheme finite type quasicoherent sheaves are locally free on a dense open set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint reduces to affine case and uses Nakayama plus reducedness to rule out nontrivial kernel elements; counterexamples exist if X is nonreduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of a finite morphism at a point
rubrics_metrics.description: For a finite morphism π: X → Y, π_* OX is a finite type quasicoherent sheaf on Y; the rank of this sheaf at p is called the degree of π at p. The degree is upper semicontinuous on Y and equals the κ(p)-dimension of the functions on the scheme-theoretic preimage π^{-1}(p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Degree is zero iff π^{-1}(p) is empty. Degree can jump; examples provided (point embedding into line).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherent modules over non-Noetherian rings: closure properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Coherent modules satisfy: coherent ⇒ finitely presented ⇒ finitely generated. The class of coherent A-modules is closed under kernels, cokernels, finite sums, images of maps from finitely generated modules, finite direct sums, and taking submodules/intersections/sums in a coherent ambient module; many of these are proved via exercises using exact sequences and the Snake Lemma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises 13.8.C–13.8.S work through these closure properties, behavior under localization, and criteria for checking coherence on a finite affine cover (D(fi)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization and checking finiteness/coherence on covers
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is finitely generated / finitely presented / coherent over A, then Mf is finitely generated / finitely presented / coherent over Af. Conversely, if (f1,...,fn)=A and each Mfi has the property, then M does too; similarly for sheaves: coherence can be checked on a cover of affine opens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use exactness of localization and patching arguments; explicit exercises (13.6.C/D, 13.8.Q–13.8.S) provide proofs and hints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction and properties of O(n) on projective space
rubrics_metrics.description: On P^1_k the invertible sheaf O(1) is defined via trivializations on standard affine opens U0, U1 with transition functions multiplication by x0/1 = x1/0^{-1}; O(n) defined similarly by nth powers of transition functions. Global sections Γ(P1, O(n)) correspond to homogeneous polynomials of degree n and dim Γ(P1, O(n)) = n+1 for n ≥ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: O(m) ⊗ O(n) = O(m + n); O(−n) is dual of O(n); example shows sheafification matters for tensor products (O(1) ⊗ O(−1) has no nonzero global sections though tensoring global sections would suggest otherwise). On P^m, similar construction via standard affine covers with explicit transition functions.
